{{nihongo|'''Yatsurugi Shrine'''|八剱神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Hakken Shrine''' (Yatsurugi Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Yagami, Kuwabara-chō, {{ill|Hashima, Gifu|Q819595|qid=Q819595}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Gifu|af|Gifu-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Gifu|ar|غيفو (محافظة)|arz|جيفو (محافظه)|az|Gifu prefekturası|azb|قیفو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Gifu|be|Гіфу (прэфектура)|bg|Гифу|bn|গিফু প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Gifu|cdo|Gifu-gâing|ce|Гифу (префектура)|ceb|Gifu-ken|ckb|پارێزگای گیفو|cs|Prefektura Gifu|cy|Gifu (talaith)|da|Gifu-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Gifu|eo|Gubernio Gifu|es|Prefectura de Gifu|et|Gifu prefektuur|eu|Gifu (prefektura)|fa|استان گیفو|fi|Gifun prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Gifu|frr|Gifu (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Gifu|gl|Prefectura de Gifu|hak|Gifu-yen|he|גיפו (מחוז)|hr|Gifu (prefektura)|hu|Gifu prefektúra|hy|Գիֆու (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Gifu|ilo|Prepektura ti Gifu|it|Prefettura di Gifu|ja|岐阜県|jv|Préfèktur Gifu|ka|გიფუს პრეფექტურა|kn|ಗಿಫು (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|기후현|lt|Gifu prefektūra|lv|Gifu prefektūra|mk|Гифу (префектура)|mni|ꯒꯤꯐꯨ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|गिफू प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Gifu|ne|गिफु|nl|Gifu (prefectuur)|no|Gifu (prefektur)|nov|Gifu Prefekture|os|Гифу (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Gifu|pl|Prefektura Gifu|pnb|ضلع گیفو|pt|Gifu|ro|Prefectura Gifu|ru|Гифу (префектура)|se|Gifu prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Gifu|simple|Gifu Prefecture|sk|Gifu (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Гифу|su|Préféktur Gifu|sv|Gifu prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Gifu|tg|Префектураи Гифу|th|จังหวัดกิฟุ|tl|Prepektura ng Gifu|tr|Gifu (prefektörlük)|tt|Гифу (префектура)|uk|Префектура Ґіфу|ur|گیفو پریفیکچر|vi|Gifu|war|Gifu (prefektura)|wuu|岐阜县|zh|岐阜县|zh_classical|岐阜縣|zh_min_nan|Gihu-koān|zh_yue|岐阜縣|qid=Q131277}}.

It is regarded as the tutelary shrine of {{ill|Nakashima district|Q24875402|qid=Q24875402|lt=Nakashima District}} in {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}} (present-day southern Hashima City). In {{ill|Kanpō|Q1145798|qid=Q1145798}} 3 ({{ill|1743|Q7580|qid=Q7580}}), thirty villages of Nakashima District in Mino Province became its parishioners<ref name="岐阜県神社庁"/>. ).

=== Overview ===
It is one of the candidate shrines (ronsha) for Ishikatana Shrine, an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Nakashima district|ja|中島郡|zh|中島郡|qid=Q780420}} in {{ill|Owari Province|ar|أواري|ca|Província d'Owari|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆوواری|cs|Provincie Owari|de|Provinz Owari|es|Provincia de Owari|eu|Owari probintzia|fa|ولایت اوواری|fi|Owarin provinssi|fr|Province d'Owari|gl|Provincia de Owari|hak|Owari-koet|id|Provinsi Owari|it|Owari (provincia)|ja|尾張国|ko|오와리국|lt|Ovario žemė|nl|Owari (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Owari|pt|Província de Owari|ru|Овари (провинция)|simple|Owari Province|sk|Owari (provincia)|sr|Провинција Овари|tr|Owari (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Оварі|vi|Tỉnh Owari|wuu|尾张国|zh|尾張國|zh_min_nan|Owari-kok|zh_yue|尾張國|qid=Q514506}}.

The place name of this area ({{ill|Yagami|Q11391710|qid=Q11391710|lt=Yagami}}) is derived from Hakken Shrine, and it is said to have been renamed from Ishida in {{ill|Jōō (Edo period)|Q1145081|qid=Q1145081}} 2 ({{ill|1653|Q6965|qid=Q6965}})<ref name="岐阜県神社庁"/>.

In {{ill|1931|Q18782|qid=Q18782}} (Shōwa 6), it became a gōsha {{Sfn|Hashima City|2004|p=663}}. On October 5, {{ill|1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754}} (Shōwa 35), it was designated a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}} (No. Kin 54) by the Gifu Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines {{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=83}}.

It shared a worship hall with Inari Shrine (enshrined deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Uka-no-Mitama-no-Kami}}; designated a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592|lt=Ginpei-sha}} by the Gifu Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines<ref name="案内板">According to the on-site information board.</ref>{{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=83}}), and they existed as separate, independent shrines (Hakken Shrine on the east side and Inari Shrine on the west side). However, in {{ill|2024|Q49619|qid=Q49619}} (Reiwa 6) July, Inari Shrine was dissolved as a religious corporation and was merged into Hakken Shrine<ref name="法人番号">{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.houjin-bangou.nta.go.jp/henkorireki-johoto.html?selHouzinNo=1200005003539|title=Information on Inari Shrine (National Tax Agency Corporate Number Publication Site)|format= |publisher=National Tax Agency|language=Japanese|accessdate=2025-07-19}}</ref>.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Ama-no-Iwato-wake no Kami|Q10940542|qid=Q10940542|lt=Kushiishimado-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Uka-no-Mitama-no-Kami}}

=== History ===
Founded in {{ill|Saikō|Q1324664|qid=Q1324664}} 2 ({{ill|855|Q25073|qid=Q25073}})<ref name="案内板"/><ref name="岐阜県神社庁">[https://www.gifu-jinjacho.jp/syosai.php?shrno=279 Hakken Shrine (Gifu Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines)]</ref>. In Jōō 2 (1653), the Inari Shrine that had been worshipped by the {{ill|Mōri Genroku family|Q11547665|qid=Q11547665|lt=Mōri Genroku family}} of {{ill|Ichinoeda|Q22124456|qid=Q22124456}} was merged into this shrine<ref name="案内板"/><ref name="岐阜県神社庁"/>.

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
* Wakamiya Shrine – transferred here in Jōō 2 (1653)<ref name="案内板"/>
* Shirahige Shrine
* Tado Shrine
* Fuji Asama Shrine
* Konpira Shrine, etc.

=== Access ===
* About a 5-minute walk from the “Yagami” bus stop on the southern route of the {{ill|Hashima City Community Bus|Q11610099|qid=Q11610099}}.
